text:
Saturday night in Toronto, and the Canadiens arrive with points in nine straight (7-0-2). Thursday was the kind of win that builds that sort of run: down two to Utah, Logan Cooley with a hat trick, and Montreal came back to win 5-4 in overtime. Here's the honest part, though. The Canadiens took 50% of the expected goals across those nine games. They're winning with balance, and with Jacob Fowler, who is at .925 and 9.7 goals saved above expected.

Nick Suzuki has points in five straight and had three in his return to the lineup, per CBS Sports. Montreal is without Ivan Demidov and Mike Matheson; Cole Caufield has taken Demidov's spot beside Juraj Slafkovský and Alex Newhook, and Zachary Bolduc has moved onto the top power play. One more to watch: our Sleeper, Josh Anderson, with 3.1 expected goals in his last ten games from the third line.

Toronto is the mirror image. The Maple Leafs are +7 in goal difference on chances worth -7.2, at 47% of the expected goals. Finishing (10.1 goals more than their chances usually produce) and goaltending have done the lifting, and in Tuesday's 3-2 loss to Utah they had only 30% of the expected goals. Kirill Marchenko is out, Easton Cowan has moved up beside Paul and William Nylander, and Jack Roslovic has a seven-game point streak. John Tavares is off ESPN's injury report, and a Daily Faceoff Toronto post put it this way: "Auston Matthews says John Tavares has been best player on the ice at practice ahead of return vs. Canadiens."

Discipline is the hinge. Montreal takes 5.38 penalties a game and draws 4.38. Our numbers lean Montreal, 3.34 expected goals to 3.18, and the playoff race already looks lopsided: 60% for the Canadiens, 16% for the Leafs. The preseason meeting went to Montreal 3-2, a game the Habs deserved only 44% of the time.
headline: Montreal's nine-game run meets Toronto's hot finishing

hunch.text: A captain's practice report, a home crowd and a goalie on the other end who has been almost too good. Our hunch: John Tavares scores in his return.
